@graph.description: Black seed (Nigella sativa), also called black cumin, is a spice whose oil is rich in thymoquinone. It has been studied mostly for metabolic health: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials in people with type 2 diabetes found that black seed supplementation lowered fasting blood glucose and HbA1c and improved total and LDL cholesterol compared with control. Most of the included trials were small and short, so the results are better read as promising than definitive. Because it can lower blood sugar, black seed may add to the effect of diabetes medications.
